A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Inverse Bridge Matching Distillation. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original IBMD-I2SB and IBMD-DDBM evaluations in Tables 1-6 and generated samples in Appendix C, alongside results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains the original IBMD evaluations and generated samples, revises several scores, and adds training-time measurements in Table 9.

M1.justification: The inverse-bridge objective, alternating updates in Algorithm 1, conditional extension, and multistep procedures are retained. The added gradient and auxiliary-model explanations do not introduce a different algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet super-resolution, JPEG restoration and center inpainting, plus Edges-to-Handbags and DIODE-Outdoor translation. The training/test sample coverage in Appendix C is retained; refreshed illustrative images do not introduce a new scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1-6 is unchanged, including DBIM, CBD, CBT and the teacher models. Updated DDIB, SDEdit and DDNM citation dates refer to the same methods. The expanded SiD discussion does not add an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported splits, evaluation sample counts, preprocessing, metrics, NFEs, multistep procedures and Table 7 hyperparameters are unchanged. The newly reported hardware and training times disclose existing configurations rather than establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a brief convergence-efficiency analysis: early training provides good-quality models, late FID improvements consume most training time, and two-step translation models converge faster than one-step models. Existing NFE comparisons and train/test overfitting analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new conditional-variance calculation concerns the training objective, not statistical uncertainty in experimental results.

E6.justification: Under unchanged reported settings, IBMD-I2SB FID/CA changes from 2.5/72.4 to 2.6/72.3 for bicubic super-resolution, 2.6/72.7 to 2.5/72.5 for pooling, 5.3/67.2 to 5.2/66.6 for JPEG QF=5, and 3.8/72.4 to 3.7/72.4 for QF=10. Tables 5-6 retain their values. New Table 9 reports training times, including 40 versus 1 hour for one-step versus two-step Handbags models and 48 versus 7 hours for DIODE models.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds a conditional-variance characterization of the minimized auxiliary loss. Section 4 adds mathematical reasoning comparing path-space KL and marginal Fisher divergence, including Equation 11 and the fixed-forward-process case. The original propositions, theorems and Appendix A proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its assertion that no universal acceleration method exists to the absence of a universal distillation method. The four stated contributions, conditional/unconditional applicability, single-step capability and abstract's acceleration claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the negatively weighted auxiliary loss as encouraging output diversity and avoiding collapse, and explains why matching marginal scores need not match bridge dynamics. Existing qualifications about training-set evaluation, teacher overfitting, DIODE test failures and memory cost remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds project code-access information. Appendix B and Table 9 newly disclose per-configuration training times on eight A100 GPUs. Existing hyperparameters, initialization, batch size, EMA and data-processing details are retained; the PDFs do not establish a change in the underlying hardware or training procedure.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands the relationship to prior diffusion distillation. Its brief model-family distinction becomes an extended comparison with already-cited SiD, arguing that marginal Fisher matching is insufficient for general unconditional bridge matching and motivating path-space KL. Bibliographic publication updates otherwise refer to existing works.

P1.justification: There are localized explanatory additions in Sections 3.2 and 4 and Appendix B, minor wording and terminology edits, updated affiliations and publication information, and new acknowledgements. The overall section structure and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9 and refreshes Figure 1, notably replacing the JPEG-restoration car example with a dog. Some appendix images are rescaled and surrounding material reflows, while existing diagrams, comparison-table structures and sample-grid layouts are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added code-access information and hardware-specific training times improve practical transparency, while the expanded explanations clarify the objective and research positioning. These are limited gains with essentially unchanged benchmark validation. The new KL/Fisher discussion also contains a local mismatch between its g(t)^2 diffusion coefficient and Equation 11's 1/(2g(t)^2) weighting, limiting the benefit of that theoretical addition.
